title: Inpatient Stays, Suspension and Breaks in Need — Hospital Beds & Support Surfaces Rentals
content:
An inpatient or skilled nursing admission suspends a Hospital Beds & Support Surfaces coverage rental, with the admission date as the suspended date; no month beginning in the suspension is billed.

**Resumption allowance (formal clause).** A suspended bed rental resumes in the same rental period only when the patient comes home no later than the class's break-in-need days after the suspension began, counting calendar days from the day after the suspended date, the allowance being the class's break-in-need days plus the days remaining in the rental month in which the suspension began.

A longer break starts a new rental period after the class's requirement for a new rental period (a new order). A private rental is never suspended; the family returns the bed or keeps paying.

The break-in-need days and the new-period requirement are the bed class's published rental-period values.

## Elements of the time rule

| Element | As the rule fixes it |
|---|---|
| Event the clock starts from | The suspension beginning — the admission date recorded as the bed record's suspended date |
| Record relied on | The suspended date on the bed record in the system |
| First day counted | The day after the suspended date |
| Unit | Calendar days |
| Length of the allowance | The break-in-need days plus the days remaining in the rental month in which the suspension began |
| Comparison | The patient comes home no later than the class's break-in-need days after the suspension began, the allowance being the break-in-need days plus the days remaining in that rental month |
| The last day of the allowance itself | Within the allowance |
| Coming home after the allowance | A longer break: a new rental period starts after a new order |

## Boundary cases

- **On the last day of the allowance.** The patient comes home on the final counted day: the rental resumes in the same rental period.
- **The day after the last day of the allowance.** The break is longer than the allowance: a new rental period starts after a new order.

## Worked illustrations (hypothetical inputs)

Inputs taken for illustration: a class with 60 break-in-need days, and a suspension that began with 12 days remaining in that rental month, giving an allowance of 72 calendar days counted from the day after the suspended date.

- The patient comes home on day 40 of the count: the rental resumes in the same rental period.
- The patient comes home on day 90 of the count: the break is longer than the allowance, and a new rental period starts after a new order.

## Points of judgement

- **Months during the suspension.** A month whose first day falls inside the suspension is not billed.
- **Private rental.** A private rental is never suspended; the family either returns the bed or keeps paying.
